Name: Builder Assistant 建筑助手
Description: Android-first Builder Assistant. v0.11.1 is a DOCUMENTATION-ONLY forensic release for multiplayer connection refusals (no code path or safety behavior changes; 379/379 offline tests and net472 0-error/0-warning Release build are unchanged from v0.11.0). Root cause was located by decompiling the target Survivalcraft.exe (x25.01.17): Game.NetWork.Packages.ConnectionRequestPackage.AcceptAclient runs SERVER-SIDE on every incoming join and unconditionally requires ModsManager.ModList (the host's loaded mods) to be a strict multiset-equal to the client's announced modInfos list — same count, same PackageName+Version per ModEntity (ModEntity.Equals), same ResourcesMd5 per ModEntity (with only PackageName='survivalcraft' skipped as a special case). If a client is missing a host mod the server rejects with '客户端没有安装服务器Mod[<Name>:<Version>]', if the client has an extra the server rejects with '服务器没有安装客户端Mod[<Name>:<Version>]', if the counts differ the server prints both lists with '[服务器]n.Name:Version' / '[客户端]n.Name:Version' and rejects with '客户端Mod数量和服务器Mod数量不一致', and if two same-name mods have differing ResourcesMd5 the server rejects with '资源包<Name>校验不通过' plus '[服务端]<md5>'/'[客户端]<md5>' lines. Game.ModInfo exposes exactly Name/Version/ApiVersion/Description/ScVersion/Link/Author/PackageName/Dependencies — there is NO server-only / client-optional / advertise=false flag, so a 'host-only mod' installation is ARCHITECTURALLY REJECTED BY SCNET ITSELF, not by Builder Assistant. Because Builder Assistant ships as a normal .netmod in ModsManager.ModList, a client that does not have the same .netmod file cannot join the host, and even a client that DOES have the .netmod file but from a different build cycle will fail ResourcesMd5. This Mod intentionally does NOT modify ConnectionRequestPackage, ResourcesMd5, ModsManager.ModList, ModEntity, ModInfo, or any network handshake surface — per AGENTS.md's rule against forging mod lists, faking validation, or skipping resource integrity checks. The two supported resolutions are: (1) Use SCNET's OWN auto-download flow — Game.NetWork.ModFileService.ModFileServer (a System.Net.HttpListener hosted by the game, listing /{modMd5}/ for each .netmod) plus Game.NetWork.ModFileService.ModFileClient.DownloadModAndJoinServer (invoked from the client's server list) fetches missing .netmod files, writes them to Utils.ModFileDirectory, then GameRestarter.RestartGame reboots so the new mod set matches; whether HttpListener can bind on Android 7723 (non-root, scoped storage) and whether the client's server-join UI actually routes to this path on Android is 待验证 (needs two real devices, and note that Utils.GetModInfoDatas enumerates ((FastDebugModEntity)ModList.Find(px => px.modInfo.PackageName=='com.fastdebug')).FModFiles, so FastDebug must be present and healthy on BOTH sides or the entire mod-list fetch returns null and the client rejects before ever reaching ModFileServer). (2) Manually install this EXACT .netmod file (same SHA-256) on every participant before joining — since Builder Assistant's world content is entirely vanilla blocks (proven offline by TestBuildEmitsOnlyVanillaBlocks) the tools simply appear in every player's inventory and the terrain is normally synced. The separate error '资源包FastDebug校验不通过' is orthogonal to Builder Assistant: it means the two devices have different FastDebug .netmod files (different 7723 build cycles, or one is public APK and the other is 7723-repack), so both sides must be provisioned from the identical SCNET 7723 package; Builder Assistant cannot and will not work around this. Prior release notes follow. v0.11.0 adds the VISUAL BUILDING WORKBENCH: a new in-hand Workbench Tool (item 904) that lets a player select, configure, preview and place a building entirely by touch, with no keyboard, no mouse hover, no desktop-only path and without editing any code. The entire interaction brain is a brand-new GAME-FREE Core/Workbench layer (a BuildingWorkbench state machine plus BuildingSelectionService and BuildPreviewModel/BuildPreviewComposer), so it is fully unit-testable offline and WorldEditRuntime was NOT rewritten. Two touch gestures drive it: tapping the SKY cycles the current knob (choose cottage / two-storey house / the currently imported clipboard blueprint; then width, length, storeys, per-floor wall height, roof hip/gabled/flat, random-seed layout variant, and quarter-turn facing), tapping the GROUND confirms the step and advances. At the Position step it computes the drop origin with the SAME arithmetic the manual build uses, then runs a strictly READ-ONLY footprint preview through the unchanged BuildPlanner and reports size, ground area, height range, main-door facing, block count and an allowed/refused verdict — it NEVER places-then-deletes a fake preview and NEVER mutates the real world to draw one. At the Build step it re-runs the planner against the CURRENT terrain and the live authority before admitting the build, so a chunk that unloaded or a block placed since the preview aborts cleanly with nothing written; the confirmed build is then handed straight back through the existing BeginBuildBlueprint -> PlanAndStart -> BuildTask -> undo pipeline, so every AGENTS safety rule (single-player-or-host authority gate, coordinate bounds, 1024/32/64 caps, main-thread-only batched writes, chunk-readiness pre-check, bounded stall, cancel, safe rollback, edit-aware undo, default no-overwrite) applies verbatim and the workbench adds NO second execution path. These guarantees are proven offline: changing a parameter or rotating AFTER a preview silently invalidates the pending confirmation (version token + stale flag); a rejected parameter change never destroys the last valid building (compose keeps the old blueprint); the preview area always equals the final build area (both come from one planner pass over the same effective blueprint); no terrain is ever written during preview; the build re-checks terrain and authority at confirm time; a remote client can never bypass the gate through the UI; and the tool never emits its own 900-904 blocks into the world. This is fully ADDITIVE: the Builder (901), Undo (902) and Blueprint (903) tools, the v0.10.0 parametric engine, blueprint import/copy, schemaVersion=2, undo/delayed-rollback and the 1024/32/64 limits are unchanged, and a new WorkbenchSession.Reset() is wired into the per-world session reset so a fresh world never inherits a stale guided build. The native x25.01.17 Dialog / ListSelectionDialog and a transparent in-world ghost renderer EXIST in the public reference assembly but are NOT yet proven usable from a Mod on the 7723 Android client, so the workbench deliberately ships with a safe toast + two-tap-gesture fallback instead of a native dialog or a ghost render; a real touch picker and Phase-2 transparent projection are marked 待验证, and unsupported UI features are never faked as usable. On-device behavior — reliable sky-vs-ground raycast discrimination, toast legibility across resolutions, item index 904 uniqueness against other mods, and host-authoritative terrain sync of workbench-built blocks to non-mod clients — remains 待验证. Offline Core + Generators + JSON + orientation + parametric-engine + workbench tests now pass 379/379 and net472 compiles 0 errors/0 warnings against the real x25.01.17 assemblies. Prior release notes follow. v0.10.1 LIFTS THE MULTIPLAYER RESTRICTION on the auto-build/undo/blueprint tools: they previously ran only in single player, but now also run when this instance is the multiplayer host (Game.NetWork.WorkType.Server). Only non-authoritative remote clients (WorkType.Client) are refused, because a client's own terrain writes are not authoritative and are not guaranteed to reach the host. This is a gate-only change — the whole plan -> execute -> undo safety pipeline, the 1024/32/64 limits and the v0.10.0 parametric engine are untouched, and a new game-free TerrainAuthority classifier makes the writable/refused decision unit-testable offline. Because generated buildings are composed ONLY of ordinary vanilla blocks that the host writes, non-mod clients who do not have this mod installed should still see the finished structures through normal chunk sync (they simply cannot see the in-hand tool blocks 901/902/903). IMPORTANT: whether that host-to-non-mod-client terrain sync actually lands on the 7723 Android build is 待验证 — it has not been proven on a real two-device session, only reasoned from the fact that the emitted blocks are all vanilla. v0.10.0 adds the PARAMETRIC BUILDING GENERATION ENGINE: instead of hand-writing block coordinates, a caller (a UI button today, a future AI tomorrow) emits one small BuildingSpec (building type, width, length, storeys, wall height, roof type hip/gabled/flat, random seed, chimney flag, window density, and a full material profile) and the engine returns a validated Blueprint through a single unified BuildingSpec -> BuildingComposer -> Blueprint entry. Generation is modular: independent Foundation / Wall / Stair / Opening / FloorPlan / Roof / Decoration components share one seeded DeterministicRandom context (xorshift32, so output is identical across runtimes) and a last-write-wins blueprint builder, and are run in a fixed order so openings carve into finished walls and the stairwell punches a landing void through a finished slab. Two building types ship: a parametric cottage (the familiar 9x11 single-storey, now with all size/roof/window parameters exposed) and a NEW genuinely two-storey house with real per-floor slabs, a load-bearing exterior shell plus a corner support beam, a walkable switchback stairwell that opens the upper floor, windows on every face, a proper gable/hip silhouette and simple interior partitions + furniture — not two hollow boxes stacked. Every spec is validated BEFORE any cell is written (min/max sizes, 64-per-axis, total height <= 64, material slots resolvable, a conservative block-count guard against the 1024-per-transaction cap, two-storey >=2 floors and >=7x7); an invalid or over-budget spec is refused outright and produces no partial blueprint and no unbounded loop. A new independent BuildingValidator then re-derives facts from the PRODUCED cells (not the components' intent) and reports structural defects — footprint mismatch, duplicate coords, unknown/unresolvable or wrong-family materials, missing or blocked/unsupported/floating entry door, broken perimeter shell, sealed-off or non-reachable interior, missing stair connection between floors, and disconnected/floating blocks — and the offline suite proves each rule actually FIRES via targeted negative fixtures rather than an over-optimistic heuristic. Seeded determinism is enforced: the same (spec, seed) yields a byte-identical blueprint, while a different seed varies door/window combos, partitions, roof decor and furniture WITHOUT breaking structural rules (never a blocked entrance, sealed room or floating block). A single game-free MaterialCatalog (logical key -> concrete vanilla type name + orientation family) is now the shared source of truth for both the runtime VanillaBlockPalette and the offline validator, so the two can never drift. This is fully ADDITIVE: the medieval cottage generator remains the registry Default with byte-for-byte unchanged output, the existing Builder (901) and Undo (902) tools, the whole plan -> execute -> undo safety pipeline (default no-overwrite of solid blocks, main-thread-only batched writes, chunk-readiness pre-check, bounded stall, cancel, safe rollback, edit-aware undo) and the 1024/32/64 safety limits are unchanged, WorldEditRuntime was not rewritten, and schemaVersion=1 JSON import compatibility is preserved (the engine emits schemaVersion=2). Offline Core + Generators + JSON + orientation + parametric-engine tests now pass 334/334 and net472 compiles 0 errors/0 warnings against the real x25.01.17 assemblies; the ON-DEVICE rendering and behavior of generated stairs/slab/fence/door buildings (stairs, half-blocks, fences, the two-cell door auto-top and stairwell connectivity) on the 7723 Android target remain 待验证 (pending real-device verification). History: v0.9.0 adds ORIENTED vanilla blocks — stairs, half-blocks (slabs), fences and doors — across all material variants, migrating the blueprint exchange format from schemaVersion=1 to schemaVersion=2. Each cell may now carry an optional family tag (f: cube/stairs/slab/fence/door) plus authored data bits (d: rotation / upside-down / isTop / four fence connection arms / door rotation+open+hinge). A new pure, game-independent Core/Blueprints/BlockOrientation codec owns all orientation math (Normalize/Rotate/MirrorX/family tag mapping) and was derived from the decompiled x25.01.17 Game assembly (StairsBlock/SlabBlock/FenceBlock/DoorBlock data accessors, Block.GetPlacementValue facing, and the SubsystemFence/Stairs/Door behavior auto-connect/auto-top logic), NOT guessed. Only orientation the block itself owns is stored: stair corner-joints and every block color are engine-derived and deliberately stripped so a blueprint never bakes state the engine would recompute differently — matching the standing no-garbage rule. VanillaBlockPalette now maps concrete type names to a family and packs data via Terrain.MakeBlockValue; the old SupportedPlainCubes set is retained as a Cube subset. Doors are a genuine two-cell block: a blueprint/copy stores ONLY the bottom half and writing it makes SubsystemDoorBlockBehavior auto-create the matching top, and the copier detects the upper half so it is skipped (never double-placed → the old 'target no longer air' abort cannot occur), and the generator already emits just the bottom, facing into the room on solid foundation. Quarter-turn rotation and X-mirror now transform authored data through the same codec (verified group law: four turns = identity; mirror = involution; door hinge flips on mirror), so copied/AI structures turn correctly. The medieval cottage generator was reworked to actually use the new families (wooden stairs eaves exercising all four facings, a wooden door, stone-slab windowsills, fence ridge finials) while overwriting existing cells so the block count and safety envelope stay within the 1024/32/64 limits. Safety model is unchanged: default no-overwrite-non-air + explicit confirm, main-thread-only batched writes, chunk-readiness pre-check, bounded stall, and undo that only restores cells the player has not since edited. schemaVersion=1 files (no f/d) still decode and load as plain cubes, so older blueprints keep working. Offline Core+Generators+JSON+orientation tests now pass 267/267 and net472 compiles 0 errors/0 warnings against the real x25.01.17 assemblies; the palette mapping and ON-DEVICE RENDERING of every stairs/slab/fence/door variant on the 7723 Android target remain 待验证 (pending real-device verification). Earlier release history follows. v0.8.2 expands the copy/build material palette with more plain stone/brick cubes: Basalt, Granite, Marble, Sandstone, Clay, Limestone and Malachite are added to VanillaBlockPalette.SupportedPlainCubes (5 -> 12), so both live-region COPY and imported/hand-authored blueprints can now reproduce these blocks. This is a whitelist-only change: the blueprint schema stays schemaVersion=1, the terrain write path still packs data=0/light=0, and entity-bearing / stateful (fluid/ice/snow) / gravity (sand/gravel) / spread (grass/soil) / unbreakable (bedrock) / oriented (log) blocks remain deliberately refused. A whitelisted name that is not a registered in-game block simply fails to resolve and the build/import aborts cleanly (it can never place a wrong block). Known caveat: PaintedCube-family members are pasted in the engine default color because per-cell color is not part of the terrain value; preserving color is reserved for a later schemaVersion=2 with a color payload. On-device RENDERING of each newly added block on the 7723 Android target is 待验证 (pending real-device verification). v0.8.1 makes import frictionless: no more creating folders or hand-writing files — copy a blueprint JSON onto the phone clipboard, tap the Blueprint Tool (903) and it paste-imports directly. The pasted text runs through a new pure BlueprintImportService that reuses the SAME BlueprintJson.Decode parser + vanilla-material pre-flight as file import (no second parser), enforces a raw-size cap, and on success auto-saves a uniquely-named, NON-overwriting copy to the library while preserving the readable (CJK) display name inside the JSON — fixing the old bug where pure Chinese names all collapsed to 'blueprint' and clobbered each other. Illegal input (empty, over-size, malformed JSON, unknown material, duplicate coords, over cap) is rejected with a precise reason and NEVER touches the current clipboard or writes terrain. The loaded blueprint is then placed with the existing Builder Tool (901) two-tap confirm through the SAME BuildPlanner/BuildTask/undo pipeline, so every safety rule (main-thread-only writes, single-player-or-host WorkType.Local/Server authority gate — remote clients refused, default no-overwrite + explicit confirm, chunk-readiness pre-check, batched apply, safe rollback/undo) is unchanged. The clipboard read is wrapped in a guarded adapter (GameInterop) because Game.ClipboardManager is a public Game.* type that is NOT part of the documented SCNET Mod API: it compiles against the verified Windows x25.01.17 assembly, but its Android/7723 runtime is 待验证, and when unavailable it falls back gracefully to the v0.8.0 toast + file-library browse. A separate reserved interface for an Android SAF file picker is stubbed but marked 不支持 (未接入) pending native-call verification. Offline Core+Generators+JSON+browser+import+naming+material-palette tests now pass 203/203, XDB merge-safety guards 7/7, net472 compiles 0 errors/0 warnings against the real x25.01.17 assemblies. v0.8.0 closed the loop 'external AI writes a blueprint JSON -> drop it on the phone -> import -> build'. New: a dedicated in-hand Blueprint Tool block (item 903). Each tap browses the Mod's blueprint library folder and loads+validates the next blueprint through the existing BlueprintJson.Decode plus the vanilla-material pre-flight; an illegal or AI-bad file (malformed JSON, over cap, unsupported block, dangling material) is rejected with a clear reason and NEVER touches the clipboard or partially imports. When the library is empty the tool prints the real library folder path (under ModsManager.UserDataPath, never a hardcoded device path) so the player can drop AI-generated .json files in with the Android system file manager. The Android file-delivery path (whether the system file manager can write UserDataPath under scoped storage) and item index 903 are 待验证 (pending real-device verification). v0.7.0 adds the generic JSON blueprint bridge that will carry future AI-generated buildings. New: a dependency-free strict JSON parser/writer (Core/Json), a blueprint exchange format (BlueprintJson, schemaVersion=1) with serialize/parse/validate round-trip, two-corner live-region COPY (BlueprintCopier) that reads real blocks into a blueprint and auto-exports it, and PASTE that rebuilds a copied or imported blueprint through the SAME BuildPlanner/BuildTask/undo pipeline as the built-in cottage so every safety rule applies identically. Blueprints persist to the Mod's own library under ModsManager.UserDataPath (never a hardcoded device path), which is also the answer to Android local-file access. Fidelity is deliberately conservative: only verified plain-cube vanilla blocks are copied/pasted; stairs, slabs, oriented logs, plants, snow, fluids and entity-bearing blocks are skipped on copy and cause a clear rejection on import/paste instead of a degraded or garbage build. Quarter-turn rotation lives in pure blueprint space. Reserved-but-unsupported fields (per-cell orientation/data/props, top-level buildOps) are rejected loudly, never faked. Undo still only restores cells the player has not since edited. The game-adapter copy/paste/import paths and all Android behavior remain 待验证 (pending real-device verification). v0.6.3 adds clear-soft and a bounded stall. Clear-soft: grass/flowers/tall grass/dead bushes/snow layers and other walk-through blocks the engine flags IsCollidable==false can now be replaced by a build, but only after an explicit extra confirmation tap — never by default; fluids (water/lava), solid terrain and player structures are still refused, and undo restores the exact original plant value. Bounded stall: our own writes can briefly drop a chunk's State below Valid during the engine re-mesh; instead of aborting and rolling back the whole cottage for that transient, the executor pauses in place and retries on the next frame, giving up (with a safe rollback) only after MaxIdleAdvanceCallsDuringBuild consecutive zero-progress calls. v0.6.2 fixed the on-device false '区块未加载' abort: editability now keys on `chunk.State == Valid AND chunk.Cells != null` (never TerrainChunk.IsLoaded) and prints real chunk coordinates. v0.6.1 fixed a shipped database-merge crash from a reused Class-parameter GUID. v0.6 keeps the independent speedboat prototype (behavior unchanged).
